# Combined interactive explorer: volcano + fissure_vent + Woods + table

Builds one shared dataset and lays out
[`interactive_volcano()`](https://mkajano.github.io/HDXBoxeR/reference/interactive_volcano.md),
[`interactive_fissure_vent()`](https://mkajano.github.io/HDXBoxeR/reference/interactive_fissure_vent.md),
[`interactive_woods()`](https://mkajano.github.io/HDXBoxeR/reference/interactive_woods.md),
and
[`significant_peptides_table()`](https://mkajano.github.io/HDXBoxeR/reference/significant_peptides_table.md)
together, all linked via `crosstalk` - selecting peptides in the table
(or hovering over a point on any scatter plot or Woods segment)
highlights the same peptides everywhere. Requires the `plotly`,
`crosstalk`, and `DT` packages.

## Usage

``` r
interactive_fissure_explorer(
  df,
  state1,
  state2,
  times,
  replicates = 3,
  alpha = 0.01,
  pvalue = 0.01,
  p_adjust = "none"
)
```

## Arguments

- df:

  output of
  [`output_tp()`](https://mkajano.github.io/HDXBoxeR/reference/output_tp.md).

- state1:

  First protein state, matched as in
  [`plot_fissure_vent()`](https://mkajano.github.io/HDXBoxeR/reference/plot_fissure_vent.md).
  Defaults to the first state found in `df`.

- state2:

  Second protein state. Defaults to the second state found.

- times:

  a single Deut.Time value to plot.

- replicates:

  number of replicates. Default `3`.

- alpha:

  alpha for the pooled critical interval. Default `0.01`. May be a
  vector (paired element-wise with `pvalue`) - if so, the volcano and
  fissure_vent panels each get their own dropdown (see
  [`interactive_volcano()`](https://mkajano.github.io/HDXBoxeR/reference/interactive_volcano.md))
  for switching between the pre-computed `alpha`/`pvalue` combinations.
  This is a native per-plot `plotly` control, not a shared one:
  switching one panel's dropdown does not move the other panel's
  dropdown, the Woods plot, or the table - a single `htmlwidget`'s
  dropdown can't reach into a separate `htmlwidget` without custom
  JavaScript, which this package does not add. The Woods plot and table
  always reflect `alpha[1]`/`pvalue[1]` (the same combination the
  cross-widget hover-highlighting key is built from).

- pvalue:

  per-peptide significance cutoff. Default `0.01`. See `alpha`.

- p_adjust:

  multiple-testing correction of the per-peptide Welch p-values, passed
  to [`stats::p.adjust()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/p.adjust.html):
  `"none"` (default) or e.g. `"BH"`, applied across the peptides of the
  comparison.

## Value

an `htmltools` tag list (a
[`crosstalk::bscols()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/crosstalk/man/bscols.html)
layout of several widgets, not a single htmlwidget) - viewable in the
RStudio viewer, embeddable in an R Markdown document, or saved
standalone with
[`htmltools::save_html()`](https://rstudio.github.io/htmltools/reference/save_html.html)
(NOT
[`htmlwidgets::saveWidget()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/htmlwidgets/man/saveWidget.html),
which only accepts a single widget).

## Examples

``` r
if (requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("crosstalk", quietly = TRUE)
    && requireNamespace("DT", quietly = TRUE)) {
file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
a <- output_tp(file_nm)
interactive_fissure_explorer(a, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound", times = "1800.00s")
interactive_fissure_explorer(a, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound", times = "1800.00s",
                              alpha = c(0.01, 0.05), pvalue = c(0.01, 0.05))
}
```
